title: Compact audit log segmentation and cost-smoothing playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: reduce hosted audit logging cost growth while preserving queryability and legal retention guarantees. Deliver a playbook and implementation for compact segmentation (micro-shards + compaction windows), adaptive TTLs tied to access heatmaps, and cost-smoothing ingest shaping so peak write costs no longer cause sustained billing spikes. Integrate RBAC v2 context metadata into logs so audit trails include the effective permission decisions and SSO correlation IDs for forensic queries.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end ingestion keeps median write latency under 120ms at 5k qps for audit events after segmentation is enabled
Monthly storage cost for audit logs reduced by >=30% on benchmark workload (realistic customer mix) without losing compliance retention windows
Searchable for common forensic queries (user:*, resourceId:*, decision:deny) across hot and cold tiers within SLA: hot <2s, cold <10s
RBAC v2 decision context and SAML/SSO session_id are present in audit schema and surface in Console trace view
Automated migration path with no data loss and a verified canary rollout plan
comments: 2026-02-22 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes: scoped to hosted and Dedicated first; Private will follow after on-prem storage adapter completed (ENG-73221). Primary knobs: micro-shard size, compaction window, per-tenant cost caps.

2026-02-28 - Ravi Patel: Benchmarked initial segmentation prototype: micro-shards (8MB target) + background compactor reduced index size by 28% on dev dataset. Observed 3% CPU increase on compactor nodes.

2026-03-02 - Priya Shah (Security): Requested RBAC v2 canonical fields (principal_id, role_set_hash, evaluated_policy_version) be added to schema. Also flagged need to encrypt PII in audit payloads at rest (KMS integration ticket ENG-75100).

2026-03-05 - Ravi Patel: Pushed RFC and sample schema to Confluence and created draft PR for ingestion pipeline (github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12890). Need final review from infra on partitioner lease model.

2026-03-08 - Infra review (Jon Kim): Suggested switching from fixed hourly partitions to a lease-based partitioner to avoid hotspotting during tenant traffic bursts. Also recommended adding a Bloom filter per micro-shard to speed negative queries.

2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel: Updated playbook to include fallback behaviour: when coldstore backfill lags, temporarily increase retention on hot tier for affected tenants and throttle low-priority telemetry. Created runbook steps for ops to revert changes.

2026-03-10 - QA (Elena Ruiz): E2E test plan in progress. Need synthetic workload generator that simulates tenant-heavy peaks and SSO session correlation. Holding acceptance until KMS encryption test passes.
risks: Compactor CPU pressure could increase infra costs if not tuned; need autoscaling and CPU sprints profiling
Schema changes require coordinated rollout across consumers (console, alerting, retention jobs); potential for missing fields during transition
KMS integration delay would force storing plaintext PII in coldstore longer than policy allows
Incorrect TTL heuristics may evict data needed for legal holds — ensure hold-override mechanism
implementation_steps: 1) Finalize audit event schema with Security input (add RBAC v2 fields and SSO correlation)
2) Implement lease-based partitioner in ingest gateway and add Bloom filter metadata to micro-shard footer
3) Add compactor service with pluggable compaction window (configurable per-tenant), and integration tests
4) Implement adaptive TTL service driven by access heatmap; expose tenant-level cost cap overrides in Console
5) End-to-end encryption integration with KMS for PII fields during compaction and coldstore writes
6) Migrate existing indices with online re-segmentation path; run canary on 2 tenants for 48 hours
7) Monitor metrics: per-tenant storage bytes/day, compactor CPU, ingest latency P50/P95/P99, query latency hot/cold
8) Post-mortem and tuning loop after canary to adjust compaction window and micro-shard sizing
rollout_plan: Canary-1: single low-traffic tenant for 48 hours; verify metrics and query correctness
Canary-2: three medium tenants and a synthetic peak generator for 72 hours; validate cost smoothing and throttles
Gradual ramp: enable segmentation for 10% of tenants per day for 10 days; monitor ops alerts
Full rollout: enable by default and flip Console knobs to allow overrides for enterprise customers
Rollback path: switch partitioner to previous fixed-hour mode and rehydrate hot tier from snapshots
